Subject: DPA & KMS requirement for FinRegCo POC

Hi Diego / Marissa,

Thanks for the fast demo last week. Procurement and InfoSec reviewed the standard DPA you shared and we have two blocking items before we can sign:

- KMS control: for regulatory reasons we need crypto-key control (customer-managed keys) retained in EU or under our KMS. Hosted SaaS with vendor-managed keys is not acceptable.
- Subprocessor visibility: we need a full, current subprocessor list and a contractual commitment to 30 days' notice for changes.

I've attached our security questionnaire for your legal team (FinRegCo-Security-Questionnaire.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a DPA + KMS approach that satisfies these two items? If not, please describe the escalation path and timing to get an exception signed by your CISO/legal.

Timeline: procurement needs a signed DPA by Oct 12 to keep the POC on track. If this is not possible, we will have to re-evaluate vendors.

Best,
Elena Morales

- Subprocessors: we will provide our current subprocessor register and commit to 30 days' notice for additions. Link to the registry and the DPA redline attached.

I've attached our redline (Redwood-DPA-redline-20261004.docx). Legal is reviewing the questionnaire and I'll loop them in. Two asks: 1) can your team confirm whether a Private pilot is acceptable for the POC, and 2) what procurement deadline flexibility do you have?

Subject: Re: DPA & KMS requirement for FinRegCo POC

Marissa / Diego —

Reviewed FinRegCo's questionnaire and your redline. Summary of legal posture and recommended approach:

- Subprocessors: we can commit to the current subprocessor list and 30 days' notice. We should add an explicit right to terminate or switch to Private deployment if undisclosed subprocessors appear.
- Data transfers: SCCs acceptable for EU transfers; we should keep the standard DPA language but add an explicit timeline for SCC deployment.
- KMS: we cannot across-the-board promise customer-managed keys for hosted customers. However, we can:
  1) Offer a limited exception for this account with bespoke contract language that commits Redwood to:
     - Restrict KMS access to a dedicated key with scoped audit logging;
     - Provide quarterly key-access audit reports to FinRegCo;
     - Allow a one-time attestation from our infra team for the POC period.
  2) Alternatively, offer a Private pilot (preferred), which fully satisfies their KMS requirement but will require provisioning and a short SOW.

Approval path: I will need written approval from CISO (Maya Srinivasan) for a KMS exception. For commercial concessions, we need Head of Sales (Marissa) sign-off and a legal-approved amendment. If you want me to draft the exception language I can — but we need an executive sign-off within 48 hours if procurement is firm on Oct 12.

Attached: legal_exception_memo.pdf (internal memo outlining the proposed exception language).

Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
